title: Right derived functors form a universal delta-functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives, $\mathcal B$ an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a left exact additive functor and $R^nv$ ($n\ge0$) its right derived functors computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive], [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. A *$\delta$-functor* from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ (Stacks Homology, Definition 010Q) [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] is a family $(G^n)_{n\ge0}$ of additive functors $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ together with, for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$, morphisms $\delta^n_G:G^n(C)\to G^{n+1}(A)$ such that $0\to G^0(A)\to G^0(B)\to G^0(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0_G}G^1(A)\to\cdots$ is exact and such that for every morphism of short exact sequences $(a,b,c)$ from $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$ to $0\to A'\to B'\to C'\to0$ one has $G^{n+1}(a)\circ\delta^n_G=\delta'^n_G\circ G^n(c)$; a morphism of $\delta$-functors is a family of natural transformations $t^n:G^n\to H^n$ with $t^{n+1}\circ\delta_G=\delta_H\circ t^n$; a $\delta$-functor $G$ is *universal* (Homology, Definition 010S) [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] if for every $\delta$-functor $H$ and every natural transformation $t:G^0\to H^0$ there is a unique morphism of $\delta$-functors $(t^n)$ with $t^0=t$. Then there are morphisms $\delta^n:R^nv(C)\to R^{n+1}v(A)$, one for each short exact sequence, making $(R^nv,\delta)$ a $\delta$-functor, and this $\delta$-functor is universal; moreover $R^0v\cong v$ naturally (Stacks Derived Categories, Lemma 015B (2), (4), and Lemma 05TE; Homology, Lemma 010T: a $\delta$-functor $G$ such that for every $n>0$ and every object $A$ there is a monomorphism $A\to B$ with $G^n(A)\to G^n(B)$ zero is universal).

proof.text: Obtain a cohomological delta-functor G and the equality G.F(n) = v.rightDerived n from exists_horseshoe_rightDerived_deltaFunctor [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor]. Its exactness and naturality already include the initial zero. The statement is existential and does not prescribe a triangle boundary, so the horseshoe construction suffices.

source.place: Lemma 05TE (1); alternative horseshoe construction: Weibel Theorem 2.4.6 and Lemma 2.2.8

proof.text: For n > 0 write n = m + 1. Embed X by the monomorphism Injective.ι X into Injective.under X [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Mathlib isZero_rightDerived_obj_injective_succ gives R^(m+1)v(Injective.under X) = 0 [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing]. Rewriting G.F using its equality with the right derived functors, every map into this zero object equals zero, so this monomorphism effaces G.F n.

Apply effaceable_deltaFunctor_isUniversal [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal] to the effacements of the preceding step. For the remaining conjunct use Mathlib rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero], valid because v preserves finite limits. Package G, its functor equality, universality and the nonempty natural isomorphism.
